card.occupation: Senior care assistant at a privately run residential care home for older people. She works mostly 12-hour day shifts, about 40 hours a week, and picks up extra shifts when the overtime rate is good.
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school in Šiauliai, Lithuania, then did one year of a vocational course in hospitality that she didn't complete. In the UK she has an NVQ Level 3 in Health and Social Care, done through work, plus the usual mandatory training certificates: manual handling, medication administration and first aid.
card.household: Lives with her husband Darius, 39, also Lithuanian, who drives a forklift at a distribution warehouse off the M62. No children. They rent a two-bed terraced house and have talked for years about saving for a deposit, without getting very far.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Šiauliai, Lithuania. Came to the UK in 2008 aged 21, first to a food-packing job in Grimsby through an agency, then to Wakefield in 2011 when Darius got work nearby. Raised Catholic. She goes to the Polish-Lithuanian Mass in Leeds at Christmas and Easter and occasionally otherwise, mostly to please her mum when she phones. She speaks Lithuanian at home and English at work. She has settled status and has never really considered going back for good, though she says she might 'when old'.
card.professional_persona: Competent and quick with residents and good at getting them washed, dressed and fed. Less keen on the paperwork side and often finishes care notes in a rush at the end of shift. She knows which shifts pay best and which managers will let things slide, and she works that to her advantage. She is not especially warm with colleagues but gets on with them. She has opinions about who pulls their weight, usually that she does and others don't.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks a lot on shift and says that's enough exercise. Darius watches basketball, the Lithuanian league and the NBA, and she half-watches with him. She tried a gym membership once and stopped going after about three weeks.
card.arts_persona: Very little interest. Watches reality TV and the odd crime drama on Netflix, and scrolls TikTok and Facebook. Has never been to a gallery in the UK and doesn't see the point. Listens to whatever is on the radio in the car.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Lithuania once a year, usually in summer, for two weeks to see her mum and sister. She likes a week in Tenerife or Turkey, all-inclusive, by the pool. Not interested in sightseeing or trying new places. She prefers somewhere she's been before and knows is good.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks simple food: potatoes, meat, soups, and cepelinai only at Christmas or when her mum visits. Buys Lithuanian sausage and bread from the Eastern European shop on Kirkgate. Says 'tea' for the evening meal like her colleagues do. Gets takeaway more than she means to, often a Chinese or a Domino's after a long shift.
hobbies_and_interests: Watching reality TV, especially Love Island and Married at First Sight
Shopping for handbags and perfume, including from TK Maxx and Vinted
Getting her nails and lashes done
Online surveys for a bit of extra money
skills: Personal care and moving and handling
Administering medication on a MAR chart
Speaks Lithuanian, decent Russian and good working English
Working long shifts without complaining much
card.career_goals: Nothing very ambitious. She'd like a small pay rise or a move to a care home closer to home with better rotas. She has thought about becoming a team leader but doesn't fancy the extra paperwork and responsibility. Mostly she wants more money for the same work and to buy a house eventually.
card.voice: Lithuanian accent, clearly not native but fluent after years here. She sometimes drops articles ('I was on shift whole weekend') and occasionally mixes up tenses. She has picked up a bit of local speech from colleagues, like 'love', 'tea' for the evening meal, 'knackered' and 'mardy', but not the full accent. Speaks at a moderate pace and keeps answers short unless she has a complaint about something. Says 'erm' a lot when thinking and uses 'you know' as a tag. If there's a silence she won't rush to fill it. She waits for the next question, or says 'that's it, really'.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, little punctuation, often skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im'). Short answers. Sometimes uses 'u' for 'you' and 'tbh'. The occasional word is spelled the way it sounds, but the meaning is always clear.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded at first. Polite but not chatty, answers what's asked and doesn't volunteer much. She can come across as slightly unimpressed or flat. She warms up a little if the topic is money, work grievances or something she's bought.
small_things: Did three long days in a row and is knackered
Got a new bag in the sale, says it was a 'proper bargain'
A resident kept calling her by the wrong name all week
The rota is changed again without asking anyone
Watching the new series of Married at First Sight with Darius
Car needs MOT and she keeps forgetting to book it
Shop on Kirkgate had good sausages in this week
deeper_things: She worries about her mum getting older alone in Šiauliai while she is far away
She and Darius have tried for a baby for a few years without luck and stopped talking about it much
She sometimes feels she's never quite belonged either here or back home
She feels a bit guilty that she earns more here than her sister, who is a teacher, and doesn't send as much home as she could
She got upset after Brexit when someone shouted at her in a supermarket car park, though she brushes it off now
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle from a coffee table, framing her from the chest up, slightly off-centre to the left. Evening light from a ceiling light and a lamp to her right gives a warm, slightly yellow tone, with some shadow under her chin. She has a round face, light skin, a faint tiredness under the eyes and a neutral, slightly reserved expression, lips closed. Her straight, dyed ash-blonde hair, darker at the roots, is pulled back into a loose ponytail. Long almond-shaped nails painted nude pink are visible as she rests her hand near her face. She wears a black zip-up hoodie over a grey T-shirt. No glasses, small gold stud earrings. Behind her: the back of a grey fabric settee with two cushions, one silver sequinned. A magnolia wall with a framed canvas print of a city skyline at night. A small wooden cross hangs near the doorframe. Part of a radiator with a towel drying on it is visible at the right edge.
